title: Quota shadowing between per-key and org-level enforcers causing missed throttles
creator: Asha Venkataraman
description: Summary: Several customers reported sudden token under-throttling (requests not being limited) while aggregate org-level usage showed bursts exceeding configured limits. Root cause appears to be a race between per-key enforcer cache eviction/rehydration and the org-level burst pool accounting, which leads to a transient ‘shadow’ counter that bypasses per-key enforcement. Impact: missed throttles (some customers exceed quota without being throttled), incorrect billing reconciliation in edge windows, and false negatives in alerting. Scope: affects hosted and dedicated control planes running runtime >= 1.20 when using hierarchical enforcement (per-key + per-org + per-route) with burst pools enabled.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Enable hierarchical rate policy: per-key limit = 100 req/min, org-level burst pool = 1000 tokens/min, enable burst allocation and cache rehydration (config flag: runtime.burst_cache.enabled = true).

2) From multiple distinct API keys (same org), rapidly send bursts that in aggregate exceed the org-level pool but individual keys alternate between bursts and idle windows (pattern: key-A burst, key-B burst, key-A idle, key-B burst...).
3) Force enforcer instance restart or trigger cache eviction for key-A during its idle period (e.g., scale down pod or call internal admin >evict-key).

4) Observe that requests from key-A after rehydration are allowed beyond per-key quota until org-level pool is reconciled — expected: per-key throttles applied; observed: no throttle for 10–30s and billing records show org-level decrement but per-key counter not reconciled.
investigation_notes: - Reproducer created in staging: see load script at https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/tree/main/quota-shadowing
- Logs: per-key enforcer logs around rehydration show 'init_counter=0' while org-pool log shows 'pool_tokens_remaining=350' — mismatch window corresponds to rehydration TTL 20s.

- Root cause hypothesis: when per-key enforcer cache is evicted, on rehydration it initializes local counter from primary metering store only if the store entry exists. Under heavy concurrent bursts, the metering store is updated primarily by org-level aggregator which writes aggregated deltas. There exists a race where the aggregator's write happens to the org pool but not yet to the per-key shard before local rehydration completes, creating a temporary gap ('shadowed' usage).

- Additional finding: batching optimization in runtime (continuous batching) collapses multiple small updates into a single org-level delta, further widening the gap between per-key persisted counters and aggregated pool writes in high-concurrency flows.
proposed_fix: 1) Add reconciliation step on per-key enforcer rehydration: read org-level deltas for keys in the same org and reconcile local counter with max(local_init, inferred_per_key_usage). 2) Short-term: disable amortized batching for metering writes for hierarchical policies (config toggle runtime.metering.amortized_writes=false) and increase rehydration backoff to reduce window. 3) Add deterministic ordering guarantee: ensure per-key shard updates are written before org-aggregator commits the pooled decrement (or write org-delta as composable operation that references per-key deltas). Implementation will include unit/integration tests and a migration job to reconcile any in-flight discrepancies for the last 5 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: - Reproducer in staging cannot produce missed throttles after fixes (scripts in load-tests pass).
- Integration test added that simulates eviction+rehydration race and asserts per-key counters never lag behind org-level pool by more than 1s in test harness.
- Monitoring: new Grafana panels and alerts added that detect per-key vs org-level counter divergence > 5% for 60s and trigger PagerDuty if customer_impact=high.
related_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4134 (toggle: disable amortized writes for hierarchical policies)
